Cat Daily Behaviour Visual Data Story

What was observed?

This visual data story explores daily cat behaviour observations collected through a Google Form. Each row records the date, behaviour type, duration in minutes, location, and time of day.

The purpose of this story is to understand which behaviours appeared most often, when they happened, and which behaviours took up the most observed time.

Behaviour frequency

A bar chart showing how often each cat behaviour was observed.

This chart shows the number of observations for each behaviour type. It helps show which behaviours were most commonly recorded in the data.

Weekday pattern

A column chart showing the number of observations by weekday.

This chart uses the timestamp variable after converting it into dates with lubridate. It shows how the number of recorded observations changed across weekdays.

Duration and time of day

A boxplot showing behaviour duration across different times of day.

This chart compares behaviour duration across different time periods. It is useful because it does not only count behaviours, but also shows how long they lasted.

Creative transformation

A creative chart showing proportion of total observed time spent on each behaviour.

For the creative component, I made two key changes to the original visualisation approach.

First, I changed the analytical focus from frequency to total time. Instead of counting how often each behaviour occurred, I calculated the total duration of each behaviour and then converted it into proportions. This changes the interpretation of the data, as behaviours that occur less frequently but last longer become more important.

Second, I changed the presentation format by combining the statistical chart with a contextual cat image using the magick package. This creates a visual data poster rather than a standard standalone plot. The image supports the theme of the data, while the chart still conveys the main statistical message.

These changes go beyond visual styling and instead modify both the data transformation and the way the results are communicated.
